title: ThermoML Property Identity & Domain Knowledge Card Schema
description: Defines the structure for per-property domain knowledge cards. One card per unique thermodynamic property (105 properties across 12 groups). Contains static identity, database usage statistics, and domain knowledge about the physical quantity — the 'textbook knowledge' about what each property measures, its physical meaning, applicable methods, and quality considerations. Analogous to MTDKS per-technique cards. Agents load these to understand a property before interpreting measurement data from INDIV block cards.

design_notes.why_per_property: Each of the 105 ThermoML properties has unique physical meaning, applicable methods, phase considerations, and uncertainty profiles. Per-property cards give agents deep context for data interpretation, quality assessment, and query planning.
design_notes.relationship_to_INDIV: ID_and_DK cards describe WHAT a property is. INDIV block cards (PCS_property_INDIV_snapshot) contain the actual measured VALUES. Agents load ID_and_DK first to understand the property, then load relevant INDIV cards for data.
design_notes.relationship_to_MTDKS: MTDKS describes HOW measurements are made (technique knowledge). PCS ID_and_DK describes WHAT is being measured (property knowledge). Together they give agents complete measurement context.
design_notes.domain_knowledge_dual_format: Like MTDKS, each card has a machine-parseable structured_block (JSON for programmatic queries) and an agent-readable description_block (prose for LLM reasoning).
design_notes.organization: 105 cards organized into 12 property group folders, mirroring the ThermoML PropertyGroup classification. Each card is a JSON file named by prop_ID.

prop_ID.description: Primary key. Slugified from the property name: lowercase, underscores for spaces, no special characters. Examples: 'mass_density_kg_m3', 'mole_fraction', 'viscosity_pa_s', 'normal_melting_temperature_k'. Unique across all 105 properties.
prop_ID.construction: slugify(prop_name): lowercase → replace spaces/commas/slashes with '_' → strip non-alphanumeric except underscore → collapse multiple underscores

identity.description: Static identity fields for this property. What IS this property?

name.description: Full property name exactly as in ThermoML (ePropName). Example: 'Mass density, kg/m3'

unit.description: SI unit extracted from the property name. Example: 'kg/m3'. Null for dimensionless properties (e.g., mole fraction, refractive index, compressibility factor).

symbol.description: Standard thermodynamic symbol. Example: 'ρ' for density, 'η' for viscosity, 'x' for mole fraction, 'Cp' for heat capacity at constant pressure.

dimension.description: SI dimensional formula. Example: 'M L^-3' for density, 'M L^-1 T^-1' for viscosity. Null for dimensionless.

property_class.description: Broad physical classification of this property

is_intensive.description: True if the property is intensive (independent of system size). False for extensive properties.

is_molar.description: True if expressed per mole (molar quantity).

is_excess.description: True if the property is an excess property (deviation from ideal mixing).

is_partial.description: True if the property is a partial molar quantity.

is_apparent.description: True if the property is an apparent quantity.

aliases.description: Common alternative names an agent or user might use. Example for 'Mass density, kg/m3': ['density', 'mass density', 'liquid density']. For 'Viscosity, Pa*s': ['dynamic viscosity', 'absolute viscosity', 'shear viscosity'].

typical_variables.description: Variables most commonly swept when measuring this property, ordered by frequency. Shows the typical experimental axes. Example for density: ['Temperature, K', 'Pressure, kPa', 'Mole fraction']. Example for mole fraction (VLE): ['Temperature, K', 'Pressure, kPa'].

var_name.description: Variable name from ThermoML vocabulary (e.g., 'Temperature, K', 'Mole fraction').

role.description: How this variable typically relates to the property: 'primary_axis' (most common sweep), 'secondary_axis' (second sweep dimension), 'composition' (mixture variable), 'environmental' (T or P held or swept as context).

usage_fraction.description: Fraction of blocks measuring this property that use this variable (0-1).

typical_constraints.description: Constraints most commonly held fixed when measuring this property, ordered by frequency. Example for density: ['Pressure, kPa']. Example for VLE mole fraction: ['Temperature, K'] or ['Pressure, kPa'].

usage_fraction.description: Fraction of blocks measuring this property that fix this constraint (0-1).

thermoml_name.description: Exact ePropName string from ThermoML vocabulary. Same as 'name'.

total_instances.description: Number of block_properties rows with this property

n_papers.description: Number of distinct DOIs measuring this property

rank_in_group.description: Rank by instance count within its property group (1 = most common)

rank_overall.description: Rank by instance count across all 105 properties (1 = most common)

common_methods.description: Top measurement methods used for this property, sorted by frequency

fraction.description: Fraction of instances using this method

common_variables.description: Most common variables (swept conditions) in blocks measuring this property

common_constraints.description: Most common constraints (fixed conditions) in blocks measuring this property

system_type_distribution.description: Distribution of system types (number of components)

domain_knowledge.description: Domain knowledge in dual format: machine-parseable structured_block + agent-readable description_block. Filled by domain expert or LLM with thermodynamic knowledge.

structured_block.description: Machine-parseable JSON with 6 sections covering the property's physical definition, measurement context, and quality considerations.

definition.description: Physical and mathematical definition of this property

physical_quantity.description: One-line description of what this property measures. Example: 'mass per unit volume of a substance'

mathematical_definition.description: Mathematical formula. Example: 'ρ = m/V' for density, 'η = τ/(dγ/dt)' for viscosity. Null for directly observed quantities.

thermodynamic_definition.description: Formal thermodynamic definition if applicable. Example: 'Cp = (∂H/∂T)_P' for heat capacity. Null for non-derived quantities.

sign_convention.description: Sign convention if relevant. Example: 'Exothermic → negative ΔH' for reaction enthalpy.

related_properties.description: Other ThermoML properties related by definition or derivation. Example for density: ['Molar volume, m3/mol', 'Specific volume, m3/kg', 'Amount density, mol/m3'].

derived_from.description: Properties from which this can be derived. Example: 'Excess molar volume' can be derived from 'Mass density' + 'Molar volume'. Empty if primary observable.

can_derive.description: Properties derivable from this one. Example: density can derive 'Molar volume', 'Isobaric coefficient of expansion' (with T-dependence).

measurement_context.description: How this property is typically measured in the ThermoML database

primary_methods.description: Standard ThermoML methods that most commonly measure this property. Maps to MTDKS technique cards.

applicable_presentations.description: Which presentation modes apply: 'Direct value, X', 'Difference with the reference state, X-X(REF)', 'Ratio with the reference state, X/X(REF)'. Most properties only use 'Direct value'.

applicable_standard_states.description: Standard state definitions if applicable (ActivityFugacityOsmoticProp only): 'Pure compound', 'Infinite dilution solute', 'Pure liquid solute'. Null for most property groups.

applicable_ref_state_types.description: Reference state types if applicable (for difference/ratio presentations). Null when only direct values are used.

phase_applicability.description: Phase and system context for this property

applicable_phases.description: Phases where this property can be measured. Subset of the global 25 phases.

primary_phases.description: Most common phases in which this property is measured. Example for density: ['Liquid']. Example for vapor pressure: ['Liquid', 'Gas'].

phase_equilibrium_type.description: Type of phase equilibrium if the property describes an equilibrium condition. Examples: 'VLE' (vapor-liquid), 'LLE' (liquid-liquid), 'SLE' (solid-liquid), 'VLLE'. Null for single-phase properties.

applicable_system_types.description: System sizes: ['unary'], ['unary', 'binary', 'ternary', ...]. Example: density applies to all; critical temperature is mostly unary.

component_specific.description: True if the property value refers to a DOI-scoped component in a mixture (for example, mole_fraction_{DOIcomp_id}). False for bulk mixture properties.

requires_solvent.description: True if the property requires a solvent specification (solution properties like molality, osmotic coefficient).

typical_ranges.description: Expected value and condition ranges from the ThermoML database

note.description: Context for the range, e.g., 'gases 0.01-10, liquids 500-2000, solids 1000-22000'

reference_values.description: Well-known reference values for sanity checking

uncertainty_profile.description: Uncertainty characteristics for this property type

typical_relative_uncertainty.description: Typical relative expanded uncertainty range. Example: '0.01-0.1%' for density, '1-5%' for thermal conductivity.

dominant_uncertainty_sources.description: Main contributors to measurement uncertainty for this property.

method_dependent_quality.description: If uncertainty varies significantly by method, list method → quality mapping

quality_indicators.description: Signs that data quality may be poor. Example for density: ['deviation from known reference substances > 0.5%', 'temperature uncertainty > 0.1 K', 'no calibration with reference fluids'].

data_patterns.description: Common data patterns observed in the ThermoML database for this property

common_block_patterns.description: Typical block structures. Example for density: ['T-sweep at fixed P (isobar)', 'P-sweep at fixed T (isotherm)', 'composition sweep at fixed T,P'].

multi_property_frequency.description: How often this property appears in multi-property blocks. Example: 'Mole fraction appears in 95% of multi-property VLE blocks'.

co_measured_properties.description: Properties commonly measured alongside this one in the same block or paper.

description_block.description: Agent-readable prose in 12 sections. Each section is a short paragraph (50-200 words) written for an LLM agent that needs to understand this property for data interpretation and quality assessment.

property_overview.description: 2-3 sentence overview: what it measures, why it matters, where it fits in thermodynamics.

physical_meaning.description: Intuitive explanation of the physical quantity. What does a larger/smaller value mean? How does it relate to molecular behavior?

thermodynamic_context.description: How this property fits into the broader thermodynamic framework. Gibbs phase rule implications, equation of state connections, relation to other fundamental quantities.

measurement_methods_overview.description: Brief overview of how this property is typically measured. Which techniques dominate? Key differences between methods. References MTDKS technique cards.

common_variable_patterns.description: Typical experimental designs: what is swept (T, P, composition)? Common constraint patterns. Expected data shapes (monotonic, with extrema, etc.).

phase_behavior.description: Phase considerations specific to this property. Which phases? Phase transitions? Equilibrium conditions? Multi-phase measurements?

data_quality_indicators.description: How to assess quality of measured values. Red flags, consistency checks, comparison with literature correlations.

unit_conventions.description: Unit standards, conversion factors, common alternative units in the literature. ThermoML's unit choice rationale.

typical_applications.description: Engineering and scientific applications. Process design, material selection, model parameterization.

common_pitfalls.description: Mistakes to watch for in data interpretation. Confusion with related properties, presentation modes, sign conventions, reference state issues.

related_properties.description: How this property connects to other ThermoML properties. Derivation chains, group relationships, complementary measurements.

reporting_checklist.description: Essential metadata an agent should check: method, phase, T, P, composition, uncertainty, presentation mode. What's needed for a complete data record?

base_prop_ID.description: [audited] Present in 100.0% of cards. Example: mass_density_kg_m3

card_type.description: [audited] Present in 100.0% of cards. Example: domain_knowledge

component_linked.description: [audited] Present in 100.0% of cards. Example: False

prop_num_id.description: [audited] Present in 100.0% of cards. Example: GLOBprop_1
